_work.title: Geheime Figuren der Rosenkreuzer — Wellcome Library plates
_work.author: Gold und Rosenkreuzer (attr. Hinricus Madathanus Theosophus / Adrian von Mynsicht)
_work.description: Geheime Figuren der Rosenkreuzer aus dem 16ten und 17ten Jahrhundert (Secret Figures of the Rosicrucians from the 16th and 17th Centuries), Altona 1785. 28 plates from the Wellcome Library's digitization, uploaded to Wikimedia Commons as 'Rosicrucian symbols from the 16th and17th Wellcome L0045259-L0045288.' The Geheime Figuren is the central emblematic compendium of the Gold und Rosenkreuzer, an 18th-century Rosicrucian order, presenting a systematic visual curriculum integrating Paracelsian alchemy, Kabbalistic mysticism, and Christian theology.
_work.blurb: Geheime Figuren der Rosenkreuzer (Secret Figures of the Rosicrucians, Altona 1785-88) is the central emblematic compendium of the Gold und Rosenkreuzer order — an 18th-century Rosicrucian brotherhood. Compiled by the order and attributed to Hinricus Madathanus Theosophus (Adrian von Mynsicht), it presents a systematic visual curriculum integrating Paracelsian alchemy, Kabbalistic mysticism, and Christian theology through elaborate symbolic diagrams encoding initiate doctrine on the three realms (Physica, Metaphysica, Hyperphysica). The most elaborately illustrated Rosicrucian text of the 18th century.
_work.rights: Public Domain. Published 1785-1788, well outside copyright.

entries.title: Three-realm cosmological circle diagram
entries.summary:
Opening diagram from Geheime Figuren der Rosenkreuzer (Altona, 1785), the foundational Rosicrucian emblematic compendium assembled by the Gold und Rosenkreuzer order. This plate from the Wellcome Library's copy presents one of the work's central cosmological diagrams structured around the three realms that organize the entire compendium: "Physica" (material world and physical alchemy), "Metaphysica" (metaphysical operations and philosophical principles), and "Hyperphysica" (divine and spiritual transformation). The Geheime Figuren claims to preserve secret symbols of the Rosicrucians from the 16th and 17th centuries, though Yates and subsequent scholars have established that it was primarily an 18th-century Gold und Rosenkreuzer production, codifying the alchemical-spiritual curriculum of that order.

## Iconographic Context
The Geheime Figuren occupies a pivotal position in Western esotericism: it synthesizes Paracelsian alchemy, Kabbalistic imagery, and Rosicrucian cosmology into a unified emblematic system. Szulakowska's work on Rosicrucian illustrated alchemy identifies this compendium as the culmination of a tradition of alchemical illustration that began with Paracelsus and was developed through Fludd, Mylius, and Khunrath.

## For artists & game designers
These plates are among the most striking visual products of Western esotericism — circular diagrams with concentric realms, hermetic figures, alchemical symbols, and German inscriptions. The three-realm structure (physical/metaphysical/divine) maps directly onto fantasy world-building frameworks. Public domain.

entries.title: Rosicrucian cosmic man / microcosm-macrocosm diagram
entries.summary:
Plate from Geheime Figuren der Rosenkreuzer (Altona, 1785), Wellcome Library copy. This plate illustrates the Rosicrucian doctrine of the human being as microcosm — the principle, derived from Paracelsus and earlier Hermetic tradition, that the human body is a small-scale image of the cosmos ("Der Mensch als Mikrokosmos"). The Geheime Figuren elaborates this doctrine with diagrams showing the correspondence between heavenly and earthly spheres, planetary rulerships of body parts, and the alchemical principles embodied in human physiology.

## Iconographic Context
The microcosm-macrocosm diagram is one of the most enduring images in Western esoteric illustration, appearing from medieval medical diagrams through Renaissance Hermeticism (Agrippa, Fludd) into 18th-century Rosicrucianism. Szulakowska traces the development of this imagery in Rosicrucian alchemy, showing how the Geheime Figuren systematized earlier traditions into a unified didactic curriculum for initiates.

## For artists & game designers
The cosmic-man figure, with its planet symbols, geometric overlays, and alchemical annotations, is one of the most visually arresting plates in all of Western esotericism. Excellent source for fantasy magic systems involving elemental/planetary correspondences. Public domain.

## Further reading
- Frances Yates, "The Rosicrucian Enlightenment" (1972)

entries.title: Prima materia / original chaos — the first matter of creation
entries.summary:
Plate from Geheime Figuren der Rosenkreuzer (Altona, 1785), Wellcome Library copy. This plate depicts the prima materia (first matter) — the undifferentiated substance from which all created things emerge in the Rosicrucian alchemical system. The Geheime Figuren's treatment of prima materia draws on both Paracelsian and Kabbalistic sources: it represents the original chaotic state before God imposed order, analogous to the tohu wa-bohu of Genesis and the primordial waters of Hermetic creation myths.

## Iconographic Context
Representations of prima materia in alchemical illustration range from dark chaotic clouds to the figure of the first matter as a hermaphroditic being, to the Azoth (Mercury as life-giving first principle). Szulakowska identifies the Geheime Figuren's prima materia imagery as part of a specifically Rosicrucian visual vocabulary developed in the late 17th-early 18th centuries.

## Further reading
- Principe, Lawrence M. "The Secrets of Alchemy" (2013)
- Szulakowska, Urszula. "The Alchemy of Light" (2000)

entries.title: Four elements diagram — earth, water, fire, air in Rosicrucian alchemy
entries.summary:
Plate from Geheime Figuren der Rosenkreuzer (Altona, 1785), Wellcome Library copy. The four elements (earth, water, fire, air) form a fundamental structure in the Rosicrucian alchemical system presented in the Geheime Figuren. This plate presents the elements in their mutual relationships — their qualities (hot/cold, wet/dry), their transformational paths into each other, and their correspondence with the three Paracelsian principles (salt, sulfur, mercury). The Gold und Rosenkreuzer curriculum required initiates to master the theory of the elements as a basis for practical alchemical and spiritual work.

## Iconographic Context
Four-element diagrams appear throughout alchemical illustration from the medieval period. The Geheime Figuren's version integrates Aristotelian elemental theory with Paracelsian alchemy and Rosicrucian spiritual doctrine, producing a uniquely 18th-century synthesis.

## Further reading
- Principe 2013, ch. 2 (elements in alchemy)
- Yates 1972 (Gold und Rosenkreuzer context)

entries.title: Tria Prima — sulfur, mercury, salt as the three Paracelsian principles
entries.summary:
Plate from Geheime Figuren der Rosenkreuzer (Altona, 1785), Wellcome Library copy. The Tria Prima — the three Paracelsian principles of sulfur (soul), mercury (spirit), and salt (body) — are central to the Geheime Figuren's theoretical framework. Paracelsus proposed these three principles as the fundamental constituents of all matter, replacing the four Aristotelian elements with a new triad that mapped onto body, soul, and spirit. The Geheime Figuren adapts this into a specifically Rosicrucian framework, integrating the Tria Prima with Kabbalistic and Christian symbolic systems.

## Iconographic Context
The Tria Prima is often depicted as three interlocking triangles, three interconnected circles, or as three figures. In the Geheime Figuren, this iconography is developed into elaborate symbolic diagrams that encode the relationships between the three principles and the stages of alchemical transformation.

## Further reading
- Principe 2013 (Paracelsian alchemy)
- Szulakowska 2000 (Rosicrucian alchemy)

entries.title: The alchemical furnace / athanor — vessels and fire of the Great Work
entries.summary:
Plate from Geheime Figuren der Rosenkreuzer (Altona, 1785), Wellcome Library copy. The alchemical furnace (athanor) and its associated vessels are central equipment of both practical alchemy and its symbolic dimensions. This plate presents the Rosicrucian conception of the alchemical laboratory as a spiritual theater, where material operations in heated vessels correspond to processes of spiritual purification and enlightenment. The furnace, bellows, crucible, and distillation vessels are shown with their allegorical meanings annotated.

## Iconographic Context
Furnace imagery appears throughout alchemical illustration, from medieval manuscripts to the 18th century. The Geheime Figuren's treatment of furnace iconography connects to its broader program of presenting alchemy as simultaneously material and spiritual practice, in the Paracelsian tradition of "Scheidkunst" (the art of separation).

## For artists & game designers
One of the richest sources for fantasy alchemy laboratory imagery. The athanor/furnace with its hierarchical fires (from base material to pure spirit) maps elegantly onto game progression systems. Public domain.

## Further reading
- Principe 2013, ch. 3-4 (laboratory practice and imagery)
- EmblemRoguelike alchemy-lab-sim for contemporary game treatment

entries.title: The seven planets and their correspondences — metals, days, organs
entries.summary:
Plate from Geheime Figuren der Rosenkreuzer (Altona, 1785), Wellcome Library copy. The seven planetary spheres and their correspondences with metals, days of the week, and organs of the human body form a fundamental structure in the Rosicrucian alchemical system. This plate presents the standard hermetic correspondence table: Saturn/lead/Saturday/spleen; Jupiter/tin/Thursday/liver; Mars/iron/Tuesday/gallbladder; Sun/gold/Sunday/heart; Venus/copper/Friday/kidneys; Mercury/mercury/Wednesday/lungs; Moon/silver/Monday/brain — arranged in a diagram that reveals their mutual relationships and alchemical significance.

## Iconographic Context
Planetary-metal correspondences are among the oldest elements of alchemical iconography, traceable to classical antiquity through Arabic alchemy into the European tradition. The Geheime Figuren's version integrates these classical correspondences with Rosicrucian spiritual doctrine, presenting the seven planets as stages of spiritual as well as material transformation.

## For artists & game designers
The seven-planet/metal system is the foundational structure of fantasy alchemy. This plate's visual presentation — often as a wheel or table with symbolic glyphs — directly inspires countless RPG magic systems. Public domain.

## Further reading
- Principe 2013 (planetary alchemy)
- Obrist 1982 (medieval alchemical imagery)

entries.title: The philosophical egg / putrefaction — the "blackening" stage (nigredo)
entries.summary:
Plate from Geheime Figuren der Rosenkreuzer (Altona, 1785), Wellcome Library copy. The philosophical egg is a central symbol in alchemical iconography representing the sealed vessel in which the Great Work takes place. The egg's closed, self-sufficient form — containing within itself the potential for transformation — makes it the ideal symbol for the alchemical process. This plate depicts the egg in its relationship to the first stage of the Work: the nigredo (blackening), when the prima materia undergoes putrefaction and dissolution before being reborn.

## Iconographic Context
The philosophical egg appears in alchemical illustration from the earliest European manuscripts through Rosicrucian works. In the Geheime Figuren tradition, it becomes a vehicle for encoding the relationship between material and spiritual transformation, the outer form of the vessel corresponding to the inner experience of the alchemist.

## Further reading
- Principe 2013 (stages of the Great Work)
- Szulakowska 2000 (egg symbolism in Rosicrucian illustration)

entries.title: The Green Lion devouring the Sun — dissolution of fixed matter
entries.summary:
Plate from Geheime Figuren der Rosenkreuzer (Altona, 1785), Wellcome Library copy. The Green Lion devouring the Sun is one of the most dramatic and puzzling images in alchemical iconography. In the Paracelsian-Rosicrucian tradition adopted by the Geheime Figuren, the Green Lion represents vitriol (sulfuric acid or antimony trisulfide) — the volatile, corrosive principle that dissolves even the most fixed matter (gold, the Sun). The image encodes both the chemical process of acid dissolution and the philosophical principle that the highest spiritual truths must be dissolved and remade.

## Iconographic Context
The Green Lion first appears in early European alchemy (Rosarium Philosophorum, 15th century) and is systematized in later Rosicrucian works. It appears in Maier's Atalanta Fugiens (Emblem 24), Mylius's Philosophia Reformata, and becomes a key emblem in the Geheime Figuren's iconographic program.

## For artists & game designers
One of the most visually striking and symbolically rich images in alchemy. A green lion with a solar orb in its jaws, surrounded by alchemical symbols — instant visual shorthand for dangerous dissolution and transformation. Public domain.

## Further reading
- Principe 2013 (Green Lion in practical alchemy)
- Abraham, Lyndy. "A Dictionary of Alchemical Imagery" (1998)

entries.title: The Phoenix — renewal through fire, the rubedo / reddening stage
entries.summary:
Plate from Geheime Figuren der Rosenkreuzer (Altona, 1785), Wellcome Library copy. The Phoenix — the mythological bird that dies in fire and is reborn from its own ashes — is one of alchemy's most powerful symbols, representing the final stage of the Great Work: the rubedo (reddening), when the purified matter is exalted to the red philosopher's stone. In the Rosicrucian system of the Geheime Figuren, the Phoenix also carries overtones of Christ's resurrection and the alchemist's own spiritual rebirth, connecting material transformation to spiritual exaltation.

## Iconographic Context
Phoenix imagery is ubiquitous in alchemical illustration, from the Donum Dei (15th century) through Maier's Scrutinium Chymicum, Flamel's illuminations, and the Rosicrucian tradition. The Geheime Figuren's Phoenix inherits all these associations, presenting it as the triumphant conclusion of the alchemical-spiritual curriculum.

## For artists & game designers
The phoenix as alchemical symbol carries different weight than the generic fantasy phoenix — it's specifically about transformation through destruction and the red/gold color of final perfection. Excellent for capstone events in game progressions. Public domain.

## Further reading
- Principe 2013 (Phoenix in alchemy)
- Szulakowska 2000, 2006

entries.title: The Pelican — self-sacrifice and circulation, the circulatory vessel
entries.summary:
Plate from Geheime Figuren der Rosenkreuzer (Altona, 1785), Wellcome Library copy. The Pelican in alchemy refers both to the mythological bird that pierces its own breast to feed its young with blood (a symbol of Christ's sacrifice and of the philosopher's self-giving) and to the alchemical vessel called the "pelican" (a circular distillation apparatus where vapor circulates continuously back into the substance). In the Geheime Figuren, the pelican appears as a symbol of the circulatio — the repeated distillation that gradually purifies and elevates the alchemical matter.

## Iconographic Context
Pelican imagery in alchemy combines Christian sacrifice symbolism with practical laboratory practice. The vessel's circular form — where the substance perpetually feeds itself — represents both the self-sustaining nature of the perfected matter and the spiritual path of self-sacrifice and renewal.

## For artists & game designers
The pelican's dual meaning (self-feeding circular vessel + sacrificial bird) gives it rich narrative potential for game mechanics involving sacrifice, cycles, and self-referential systems. Public domain.

entries.title: The Red Lion — the perfected matter, the rubedo, solar exaltation
entries.summary:
Plate from Geheime Figuren der Rosenkreuzer (Altona, 1785), Wellcome Library copy. If the Green Lion represents the corrosive, volatile principle that dissolves matter, the Red Lion represents its purified, fixed, exalted form — the matter at the stage of rubedo (reddening), approaching the condition of the philosopher's stone. In the Paracelsian-Rosicrucian system, the Red Lion is associated with the fixed principle, with gold, with the Sun in its highest aspect, and with the spiritual qualities of courage, will, and illumination.

## Iconographic Context
The contrast between the Green Lion (volatile/dissolving) and the Red Lion (fixed/perfecting) encodes the fundamental alchemical dialectic between dissolution and coagulation. The Geheime Figuren's presentation of these two lions draws on the tradition established in the Rosarium Philosophorum and elaborated through Maier, Mylius, and the Rosicrucian emblem tradition.

entries.title: Arbor Philosophica / Alchemical Tree — the Tree of the Philosophers
entries.summary:
Plate from Geheime Figuren der Rosenkreuzer (Altona, 1785), Wellcome Library copy. The Tree of Philosophy (Arbor Philosophica) is one of the central organizing images of the alchemical tradition, representing the growth and development of the philosopher's stone from its roots in the prima materia through the stages of the Great Work to the fruit of perfection. In the Geheime Figuren, the alchemical tree typically shows different alchemical substances, processes, or virtues growing as branches and fruits from the philosophical earth of the first matter.

## Iconographic Context
The arbor tradition in alchemy is ancient and multivalent. Llullian Trees of Knowledge (13th-14th century) provided the template; alchemists adapted the image to map the stages of transmutation. In Rosicrucian alchemy, the tree also carries Kabbalistic associations with the Sephirotic Tree of Life, integrating Christian, alchemical, and Kabbalistic symbolism.

## For artists & game designers
The alchemical tree provides a perfect visual metaphor for skill trees, technology trees, and research trees in game design. The Geheime Figuren version is particularly elaborate and visually rich. Public domain.

entries.title: Adam in the earth / Adam as the philosophical man
entries.summary:
Plate from Geheime Figuren der Rosenkreuzer (Altona, 1785), Wellcome Library copy. Adam in the alchemical tradition embodies the first perfection of creation before the Fall — and the goal of the alchemist is to restore matter to that Adamic perfection. The Geheime Figuren's treatment of Adam draws on both the Kabbalistic Adam Kadmon (primordial man containing all creation within himself) and the Paracelsian concept of the philosopher as "second Adam" who completes the work of creation through alchemy.

## Iconographic Context
Adamic imagery in alchemy connects to Paracelsianism, Kabbalism, and Rosicrucian doctrine. Szulakowska identifies the Geheime Figuren's Adam imagery as part of a systematic synthesis of these traditions into a unified esoteric curriculum.

entries.title: The Sun and Moon conjunction — the alchemical marriage of opposites
entries.summary:
Plate from Geheime Figuren der Rosenkreuzer (Altona, 1785), Wellcome Library copy. The conjunction of the Sun (Sol, gold, the fixed principle, the king) and the Moon (Luna, silver, the volatile principle, the queen) is one of the most fundamental images in alchemical iconography. The Chymical Wedding of Sol and Luna — the union of opposites — represents the key step in the Great Work where the fixed and volatile principles are united, producing the philosophical mercury from which the stone will crystallize. The Geheime Figuren gives this conjunction a specifically Rosicrucian framing, connecting it to themes of divine marriage and spiritual union.

## Iconographic Context
The Sun-Moon conjunction appears in the Rosarium Philosophorum (the most influential illustrated alchemical text), in Maier's Atalanta Fugiens, in Mylius's Philosophia Reformata, and throughout the Rosicrucian tradition. The Geheime Figuren synthesizes all these depictions.

## For artists & game designers
The solar-lunar opposition and union is one of the richest visual vocabularies in esotericism — gold vs. silver, fire vs. water, masculine vs. feminine, day vs. night. Excellent for visual storytelling about balance and integration.

entries.title: Azoth / Philosophical Mercury — the universal solvent and life principle
entries.summary:
Plate from Geheime Figuren der Rosenkreuzer (Altona, 1785), Wellcome Library copy. Azoth (from Arabic "az-zā'ūq," via Latin "azoth") denotes the philosophical mercury — the universal first principle, the "A to Z" of alchemical knowledge, and the life-giving spirit that animates all matter. In the Paracelsian-Rosicrucian tradition of the Geheime Figuren, Azoth is often depicted as a hermaphroditic angelic figure at the center of a cosmological diagram, combining male and female, solar and lunar, spiritual and material principles.

## Iconographic Context
The most famous Azoth image is the "Azoth of the Philosophers" (1659), often attributed to Basil Valentine, showing the androgynous Azoth figure with wings, a caduceus, and standing on a moon within a circle of the seven planetary figures. The Geheime Figuren's Azoth imagery draws on this tradition, adapting it for the Gold und Rosenkreuzer curriculum.

## For artists & game designers
The Azoth figure — often androgynous, winged, combining multiple symbolic systems — is one of the most visually powerful images in Western esotericism. Excellent source material for divine or transcendent entities in fantasy settings.

entries.title: The philosopher's stone — lapis philosophorum, the goal of the Great Work
entries.summary:
Plate from Geheime Figuren der Rosenkreuzer (Altona, 1785), Wellcome Library copy. The philosopher's stone (lapis philosophorum) — the mysterious substance that transmutes base metals into gold and confers spiritual perfection on the alchemist — is presented here in its symbolic dimensions. The Geheime Figuren's treatment of the stone is typical of late Rosicrucian alchemy: the stone is understood as simultaneously a physical substance achievable through laboratory practice and a spiritual principle that transforms the practitioner's soul. The stone is often depicted as a red or white cubic form, sometimes as a luminous gem, sometimes as a small human figure ("homunculus").

## Iconographic Context
The philosopher's stone is the defining goal of all alchemy and receives extensive visual treatment throughout the tradition. The Geheime Figuren's version integrates the standard iconography with specifically Rosicrucian doctrine about spiritual transformation and divine illumination.

## For artists & game designers
The philosopher's stone as visual symbol is enormously flexible — it can be depicted as a red gem, a glowing cube, a living small person, or an abstract form. The Geheime Figuren gives it its most systematically developed symbolic context. Public domain.

entries.title: Divine Triangle / Sacred Geometry — the geometric foundation of creation
entries.summary:
Plate from Geheime Figuren der Rosenkreuzer (Altona, 1785), Wellcome Library copy. Sacred geometry plays a central role in the Geheime Figuren's cosmological system, as it does throughout the Rosicrucian tradition derived from Fludd and earlier sources. This plate presents geometric forms — circles, triangles, squares, and their combinations — as encoding the fundamental structures of creation. The triangle in particular represents the Trinity (Christian), the Tria Prima (Paracelsian), and the three realms (Physica/Metaphysica/Hyperphysica) of the Geheime Figuren itself.

## Iconographic Context
Sacred geometry in Western esotericism derives from Platonic and Neoplatonic sources (the Timaeus), was developed in Renaissance Hermeticism (Ficino, Pico, Agrippa), and reached its fullest alchemical elaboration in Fludd's cosmic-geometric diagrams. The Geheime Figuren inherits this tradition, adapting it for the Gold und Rosenkreuzer curriculum.

entries.title: Cosmic creation diagram — the emergence of the world from divine light
entries.summary:
Plate from Geheime Figuren der Rosenkreuzer (Altona, 1785), Wellcome Library copy. This plate presents one of the Geheime Figuren's cosmogonic diagrams — showing the emergence of the created world from the divine principle ("Das ewige Licht," the eternal light, in Rosicrucian terminology). The Gold und Rosenkreuzer developed an elaborate cosmology integrating Christian creation theology with Kabbalistic emanation doctrine and Neoplatonic metaphysics, all encoded in symbolic diagrams of increasing complexity.

## Iconographic Context
Cosmogonic diagrams in Rosicrucian alchemy draw on Fludd's "Historia Macrocosmi et Microcosmi" (1617-1621), Khunrath's "Amphitheatrum Sapientiae Aeternae" (1595), and Leibniz-era speculative philosophy. The Geheime Figuren synthesizes these sources into a systematic visual theology.

entries.title: The Rosicrucian adept / initiate — the practitioner of the Great Work
entries.summary:
Plate from Geheime Figuren der Rosenkreuzer (Altona, 1785), Wellcome Library copy. The figure of the Rosicrucian adept — the initiated practitioner of the alchemical-spiritual path — appears in the Geheime Figuren as both an idealized form and a practical guide. This plate presents the adept in their ritual or contemplative posture, surrounded by the symbols of their work and the attributes of their knowledge. The Gold und Rosenkreuzer system, which produced the Geheime Figuren, was organized into degrees of initiation, each corresponding to a level of alchemical-spiritual attainment. The adept figure encodes these degrees visually.

## Iconographic Context
The figure of the hermit-philosopher-adept has a long history in alchemical illustration, from the illuminator of Ripley Scrolls through the Rosicrucian tradition. The Geheime Figuren's adept figure synthesizes this tradition with specifically 18th-century concerns about rationalism, pietism, and esoteric initiation.

entries.title: Angelic figure — the divine messenger between worlds
entries.summary:
Plate from Geheime Figuren der Rosenkreuzer (Altona, 1785), Wellcome Library copy. Angelic and divine figures appear throughout the Geheime Figuren, encoding the Rosicrucian doctrine of celestial intermediaries between the material world and the divine source. In the Gold und Rosenkreuzer system, angels mediate between the three realms (Physica, Metaphysica, Hyperphysica), communicating divine light and enabling the alchemist's spiritual ascent. These figures often combine attributes from Christian angelology with hermetic and Kabbalistic angel-lore.

## Iconographic Context
Angel imagery in alchemical illustration integrates multiple traditions: Christian iconography, Pseudo-Dionysian celestial hierarchies, Kabbalistic angelic orders, and the hermetic concept of "daimon" as mediating spirit. The Geheime Figuren's angels are particularly elaborate, often depicted with wings, planetary attributes, and symbolic implements.

entries.title: The Ouroboros — the serpent eating its tail, eternal return and circular time
entries.summary:
Plate from Geheime Figuren der Rosenkreuzer (Altona, 1785), Wellcome Library copy. The Ouroboros — the snake or dragon eating its own tail — is one of the oldest and most universal symbols in world myth and one of the defining images of alchemical iconography. In the Geheime Figuren, the Ouroboros encodes multiple meanings simultaneously: the circular self-sufficiency of the alchemical process (which ultimately feeds itself); the eternal return of creation and dissolution; the unity of beginning and end; and the prima materia as the "one thing" that contains and transforms itself. The Rosicrucian system of the Geheime Figuren connects these meanings to the doctrine of divine eternity.

## Iconographic Context
The Ouroboros appears in ancient Egyptian and Greek alchemy (Chrysopoeia of Cleopatra, 3rd c. CE), in the Byzantine and Arabic alchemical tradition, and throughout European alchemical illustration from the medieval period. The Geheime Figuren's Ouroboros integrates these earlier appearances with specifically Rosicrucian cosmic doctrine.

## For artists & game designers
The Ouroboros is one of the most immediately recognizable symbols in all esotericism — endlessly flexible for representing cycles, self-reference, infinity, and cosmic order. Public domain.

entries.title: The Dove — the Holy Spirit descending, divine breath animating matter
entries.summary:
Plate from Geheime Figuren der Rosenkreuzer (Altona, 1785), Wellcome Library copy. The dove in Rosicrucian alchemy represents the Holy Spirit (Spiritus Sanctus) — the divine breath that animates matter and enables spiritual transformation. In the Geheime Figuren's theological framework, the alchemical process is understood as a collaboration between the human practitioner and divine grace, with the dove/Holy Spirit descending to quicken the inert matter and enable its elevation to the philosopher's stone. This connects alchemy to Christian pneumatology and to the Paracelsian concept of "Gastein" or "Archeus" — the vital spirit within matter.

## Iconographic Context
The dove appears throughout Christian alchemical iconography, from the illuminations of the Rosarium Philosophorum through the Rosicrucian emblem tradition. In the Geheime Figuren, it appears in the context of the "Great Conjunction" — the union of divine and material principles.

entries.summary: Plate from Geheime Figuren der Rosenkreuzer (Altona, 1785), Wellcome Library copy. The golden vessel or chalice that receives the philosopher's stone represents the final perfection of the alchemical vessel — itself transformed, like its contents, into pure gold. In the Geheime Figuren's eschatological framework, the golden vessel also carries overtones of the Holy Grail (the vessel of divine wisdom and spiritual nourishment) and the Kabbalistic Kli (vessel of divine light). The Gold und Rosenkreuzer curriculum understood the perfected vessel as a symbol of the transformed initiate who can now receive and contain divine illumination.

entries.title: The waters of creation / the firmament separating upper and lower waters
entries.summary:
Plate from Geheime Figuren der Rosenkreuzer (Altona, 1785), Wellcome Library copy. The waters of creation — the primordial waters of Genesis separated by the divine act into upper (heavenly) and lower (earthly) waters — provide the Geheime Figuren's cosmogonic framework. In the Paracelsian-Rosicrucian reading, the separation of the waters is an alchemical act: God as the first alchemist separating and purifying creation from chaos. This doctrine connects alchemy to theology and makes the alchemist's laboratory work a participation in the ongoing creative activity of God.

## Iconographic Context
Creation imagery in Rosicrucian alchemy draws on Genesis commentary, Kabbalistic accounts of creation (Bereshit Rabbah, Zohar), and Hermetic cosmogony. The Geheime Figuren synthesizes these into a visual cosmogony that serves as the theoretical foundation for the practical alchemical curriculum.

entries.title: The Star of the Philosophers — the guiding light of wisdom
entries.summary: Plate from Geheime Figuren der Rosenkreuzer (Altona, 1785), Wellcome Library copy. The Star of the Philosophers (Stella Philosophorum) guides the alchemist through the darkness of the Great Work, representing both the light of wisdom that illuminates the path and the star-like radiance of the philosopher's stone at the culmination of the process. In the Rosicrucian system of the Geheime Figuren, the Stella Philosophorum is also associated with Venus/Lucifer as the morning star announcing the new day of spiritual dawn, and with the Star of Bethlehem guiding the Magi (alchemist-philosophers) to the goal.

entries.title: The Rainbow / Covenant — divine promise and the spectrum of light
entries.summary:
Plate from Geheime Figuren der Rosenkreuzer (Altona, 1785), Wellcome Library copy. The rainbow in Rosicrucian alchemy represents both the divine covenant (the Noahic rainbow as divine promise) and the refraction of divine light into its constituent colors — the spectrum that reveals the inner nature of white light. In the alchemical framework, the rainbow corresponds to the "peacock's tail" (cauda pavonis) — the iridescent display of colors that appears in the alchemical vessel just before the whitening (albedo) stage. The Geheime Figuren uses the rainbow to connect this alchemical stage to its cosmic and theological significance.

## Iconographic Context
The peacock's tail and rainbow imagery appears in medieval Islamic alchemy (Jabir ibn Hayyan), enters European alchemy through the Arabic tradition, and receives its most elaborate development in the Rosicrucian works of the 17th-18th centuries.

entries.title: The final emblem — completion of the Great Work and spiritual illumination
entries.summary:
Final plate from Geheime Figuren der Rosenkreuzer (Altona, 1785), Wellcome Library copy. This concluding plate of the Wellcome sequence presents the completion of the Rosicrucian alchemical-spiritual curriculum — the achievement of the Great Work in its material dimension (the philosopher's stone) and its spiritual dimension (the illuminated initiate). The Gold und Rosenkreuzer curriculum organized around the Geheime Figuren culminated in the highest degrees of initiation, where the practitioner was understood to have achieved something analogous to the philosopher's stone in their own soul.

## Iconographic Context
The Geheime Figuren's concluding imagery draws together the strands of the entire work: the three realms (Physica, Metaphysica, Hyperphysica), the alchemical stages (nigredo, albedo, rubedo), and the Rosicrucian theological framework, bringing them to a synthetic conclusion that encodes the complete doctrine of the Gold und Rosenkreuzer in a single emblem.

## For artists & game designers
The concluding plate of a systematic alchemical-spiritual curriculum — ideal for final boss rooms, endgame revelations, or capstone scenes in mystery/esoteric narratives. Public domain.
